thesis: The Philippine Stock Exchange, Inc. operates the national equity market and related market infrastructure in the Philippines. **[Fact]** It earns fees on stock listings, trading (transaction fees billed at 0.005% of peso trade value), market data, depository services, and clearing through subsidiaries including Philippine Dealing System Holdings Corp. (PDSHC), Philippine Depository & Trust Corp. (PDTC), and Philippine Dealing & Exchange Corp. (PDEx) (`quarterly_report_3q_2025.pdf`). **[Fact]** FY2025 consolidated gross revenue was **PHP 2.84 billion** and net income after tax **PHP 1.22 billion**; parent-attributable earnings per share were **PHP 14.11** (`annual_report_2025.pdf`). **[Fact]** At **PHP 211.00** per share (PSE edge, 2026-06-09), the stock trades near **15 times** our **PHP 14.00** normalized owner-cash starting point.
why_market_wrong: There is no dated structural discount. **[Inference]** Investors may treat the 2025 revenue step-up (gross revenue doubled year on year after PDSHC consolidation) as pure organic growth rather than a partly inorganic stack change, and may underweight the recurring **PHP 10** annual dividend (roughly **4.7%** yield at spot). **[Inference]** Conversely, the market may be right that post-consolidation scale and Philippines capital-market depth justify a mid-teens earnings multiple without a further rerating catalyst. Return is franchise earnings power at price, not a timed mispricing with a known payoff date.
